check.question: Which ticket IDs were open or pending at the end of March 31, 2026, and closed at the end of April 30, 2026?
check.sql:
WITH march_state AS (
  SELECT t.ticket_id,
         COALESCE((
           SELECT se.to_status
             FROM ticket_events e
             JOIN ticket_status_events se ON se.event_id = e.event_id
            WHERE e.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
              AND e.occurred_at < '2026-04-01 00:00:00'
            ORDER BY e.occurred_at DESC, e.seq DESC
            LIMIT 1
         ), 'open') AS status
    FROM tickets t
   WHERE t.created_at < '2026-04-01 00:00:00'
),
april_state AS (
  SELECT t.ticket_id,
         COALESCE((
           SELECT se.to_status
             FROM ticket_events e
             JOIN ticket_status_events se ON se.event_id = e.event_id
            WHERE e.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
              AND e.occurred_at < '2026-05-01 00:00:00'
            ORDER BY e.occurred_at DESC, e.seq DESC
            LIMIT 1
         ), 'open') AS status
    FROM tickets t
   WHERE t.created_at < '2026-05-01 00:00:00'
)
SELECT m.ticket_id
  FROM march_state m
  JOIN april_state a ON a.ticket_id = m.ticket_id
  JOIN ticket_statuses s ON s.status_code = m.status
 WHERE s.counts_as_backlog = 1
   AND a.status = 'closed';
check.wrong_sql:
-- Wrong assumption: 'has a status_changed to closed before the April cutoff' is treated as 'closed at the April cutoff'.
-- It ignores a reopening that happens at the SAME timestamp as the closure but with a higher seq.
WITH march_state AS (
  SELECT t.ticket_id,
         COALESCE((
           SELECT se.to_status
             FROM ticket_events e
             JOIN ticket_status_events se ON se.event_id = e.event_id
            WHERE e.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
              AND e.occurred_at < '2026-04-01 00:00:00'
            ORDER BY e.occurred_at DESC, e.seq DESC
            LIMIT 1
         ), 'open') AS status
    FROM tickets t
   WHERE t.created_at < '2026-04-01 00:00:00'
)
SELECT m.ticket_id
  FROM march_state m
  JOIN ticket_statuses s ON s.status_code = m.status AND s.counts_as_backlog = 1
 WHERE EXISTS (
         SELECT 1
           FROM ticket_events e
           JOIN ticket_status_events se ON se.event_id = e.event_id
          WHERE e.ticket_id = m.ticket_id
            AND se.to_status = 'closed'
            AND e.occurred_at >= '2026-04-01 00:00:00'
            AND e.occurred_at < '2026-05-01 00:00:00'
       );
check.witness: Ticket 2 is the discriminator. At the March cutoff (occurred_at < 2026-04-01 00:00:00) ticket 2 is still open (its transfer 10->50 and both status changes sit exactly at 2026-04-01 00:00:00, the exclusive bound, so it is in the March backlog under team 10). In the April replay, event seq 3 closes it open->closed at 2026-04-01 00:00:00, and event seq 4 reopens it closed->open at the SAME timestamp with a higher seq. Replaying in (occurred_at, seq) order leaves ticket 2 open at the April cutoff, so gold SQL returns only ticket 1 (pending in March via seq 2 at 2026-03-10 10:00:00, then pending->closed at 2026-04-01 00:00:00 seq 3, still closed at the April cutoff). wrong_sql sees ticket 2's close event in April and wrongly returns {1, 2}. Ticket 3 also closes/reopens repeatedly but ends open at both cutoffs. No other ticket has an April status_changed to closed. Literal rows derived by hand-replay of the frozen fixture; ordered=False, so no row order is implied.
